deviationsFromPlan: Steady-state prune tracks the names ProcessManager itself wrote (paneSecretFiles) instead of listing <state_dir>/secrets on every persist(): the plan's per-save readdir added real fs I/O to every save, which made processes.test.ts fixtures that fake `sleep` (deadline timers fire instantly) race against the launch chain and flake; the boot-time prune (index.ts → ProcessManager.pruneSecretFiles) still lists the directory and reaps crash leftovers. Same observable contract: a file is removed by the persist that follows its locator being cleared.

Prune acceptance test drops the plan's `sleep: async () => {}` override: with a no-op sleep the controller registration deadline fires immediately and retires the just-spawned controller, deleting the very locator the test asserts on. The default fake WorkerRpcClient closes gracefully, so closeTree needs no fake timeout.

One pre-existing test (`does not drop a queued idle-resume assignment as stale…`) awaited a single `Bun.sleep(0)` after emitting idle; it now awaits the persist that records the dequeue via a saveState override — the promotion drain's persist is no longer a pure microtask chain.

round2.deviationFromReviewSuggestion: C2: the boot-token write stays BEFORE the per-issue serialize lane (inside the owner's hold), not inside it. Reason: the only deterministic reproduction of the defect — the reviewer's own — observes generation 2's write landing before generation 1 settles; with the write inside the lane that write is queued behind generation 1's blocked tmux call, so the reproduction deadlocks post-fix and no test can fail pre-fix / pass post-fix. Placement adds no correctness the refcount does not: same-token writes and opens are already FIFO in the canonical park-then-re-admit order, and a reverse-order generation (gen 2 entering the lane before gen 1 at all) would clobber gen 2's token with gen 1's in either placement — that exotic case is unchanged from round 1 and noted for the architect below.

observationsForArchitect: Reverse-order root generations (a generation-2 spawnRoot reaching the per-issue lane before generation 1 does — e.g. generation 1 still in provisionWorkspace when the park-then-re-admit lands) would open pane 2 and then let generation 1's later write clobber the shared architect secret file before pane 2 reads it (pane 2 then 403s at /process/started on the generation check and is retired by the registration deadline). Not reachable in the documented scenario (generation 1 is blocked inside the lane when generation 2 is created) and unaffected by write placement; the fix would be a stale-at-lane-entry guard in launchShimmedProcess plus a spawnTree return path that stores nothing — larger than this round's findings.
